title: Async checker default check_revocation_against_anchor=Ok(()) footgun
description: Replicates the known RevocationChecker default-skip footgun in the async trait. Old: PKIX-f1j4.5
close_reason:
The concrete footgun is closed and tested everywhere. All six wrapper types override check_revocation_against_anchor -- HttpCrlFetcher, HttpOcspFetcher, CachedHttpCrlFetcher, CachedHttpOcspFetcher (review_http.rs) and AsyncHttpCrlFetcher, AsyncHttpOcspFetcher (review_async_anchor.rs) -- and each has its own test, which is necessary because the default is inherited per impl and a dropped override on any one type silently reopens the hole. Verified all six pass.

The trait default itself stays. AsyncRevocationChecker mirrors pkix_revocation::RevocationChecker deliberately, which that module's design notes give as the reason for the parallel trait family ('consumers that want both async and sync support can write thin parallel implementations'); both traits carry the security warning on the method and in their 'Implementing this trait' section. Removing only the async default would make the two diverge for no gain, and removing both is a decision about pkix-revocation's public API rather than this crate's hardening -- file it there if wanted.

Also corrected a stale comment in review_http.rs that said four wrapper types where there are six. Commit 7ddf44f8.
